title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page is headed 'Structures d'effectivité'. This page is item 7°) in a list of the structures carried by the (conjectural, Tannakian) category M of motives with motivic Galois group G. Item 7°) is the effectivity structure.

Step 1 (the definition). An effectivity structure is a strictly full subcategory M^+ ⊂ M, the 'effective motives', with these properties:
- it is stable under ⊗, under direct sums and under subobjects (a crossed-out word suggests he first wrote 'sous-quotients'; in a semisimple category the two notions coincide);
- the Lefschetz/Tate motive Λ(-1) is effective (this is an insertion);
- every E becomes effective after a Tate twist: there is n with E(-n) = E ⊗ Λ(-1)^{⊗n} in M^+.
In modern terms, M is recovered from M^+ by inverting the Lefschetz motive: M = M^+[L^{-1}].

Step 2 (translation to the group). Grothendieck notes that such a structure is the same thing as data on G_ℂ (the motivic Galois group), and conversely. Since M is semisimple and M^+ is stable under ⊕ and subobjects, M^+ is determined by its set of irreducible objects. So the structure is equivalent to a cone K^+(G) ⊂ K(G), the Grothendieck ring of representations. This cone:
- contains 0;
- is stable under addition and multiplication;
- is generated by classes of irreducibles and is saturated for constituents;
- contains the class of Λ(-1), with the twisting condition above.
A marginal insertion seems to refer to 'l'anneau des ... /ℚ', i.e. working with ℚ-rational representations (irreducible over ℚ).

Step 3 (further axioms). He says other axioms should be imposed. For example, for the Hodge realization H, every effective E should have Hodge gradation in nonnegative degrees: h^{p,q} ≠ 0 only for p, q ≥ 0. A boxed tentative axiom reads roughly: 'for each i there is only [a finite number?] of types of effective motives of weight i ... in particular ... G^0'. It is followed by a circled '(??)', marking his own doubt.

Step 4 (effective cocharacters). A homomorphism i: G_{m,ℂ} → G_ℂ is called 'effectif' (he first wrote 'positif') if, for every E ∈ Ob M^+, the induced grading of E_ℂ is in nonnegative degrees. The Hodge cocharacter of an effective motive should be of this kind.

Step 5 (margins).
- The left margins appear to require that the gradations be compatible with rationality: a cone over ℚ, irreducibility over ℚ.
- They also appear to require that the effectivity structure be of a type determined by, or compatible with, the identity component G^0.

Purpose: to encode the notion 'effective motive' purely in Tannakian/group-theoretic terms (G, K(G), cocharacters), as part of a list of the structures the motivic Galois group should carry. This is preparation for formulating the Hodge/Tate/standard conjectures group-theoretically.

The page's mathematics is unrelated to the next page (a typed page on Azumaya algebras / Brauer group).
errors: The equivalence 'effective subcategory ↔ cone in K(G)' needs semisimplicity of M (or stability under subquotients, not just subobjects). Grothendieck hesitated between 'sous-quotients' and 'sous-objets'; in the semisimple setting this is harmless.

The tentative boxed axiom is marked '(??)' by Grothendieck. If it means finitely many effective motives of weight i up to isomorphism, it is false: there are infinitely many non-isogenous elliptic curves in weight 1. If 'type' means Hodge type, it is trivially true, since p+q=i with p, q ≥ 0. His doubt is justified either way.

A cone in K(G) alone does not obviously encode stability under subobjects. One must also require that it be saturated, i.e. generated by the irreducibles it contains. The page does not state this explicitly.

ideas.what: Effective motives as a ⊗-stable, ⊕-stable, subobject-stable full subcategory M^+ of motives, containing the Lefschetz motive, from which all motives are obtained by Tate twisting.
ideas.modern_name: Effective motives; M = M^eff[L^{-1}] (inverting the Lefschetz/Tate object)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1960s, via Manin 1968, Demazure, Kleiman); Voevodsky for DM^eff → DM (1990s–2000)
ideas.where_published: Described in Manin's and Kleiman's expositions of Grothendieck's motives; Saavedra Rivano's thesis (1972) treats Tannakian aspects

ideas.what: Encoding the effectivity structure as a cone K^+(G) in the representation ring of the motivic Galois group, stable under sum and product.
ideas.modern_name: Positivity/effectivity sub-semiring of K(Rep G); equivalently a tensor subcategory of Rep(G) closed under subquotients but not duals, i.e. a monoid scheme with unit group G (Tannaka duality for monoids)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tannakian reconstruction for monoids: Saavedra Rivano (1972) in part; reductive monoids (Putcha, Renner, Vinberg, 1980s–90s); not standardly applied to effective motives

ideas.what: Effective cocharacters G_m → G_ℂ: those inducing nonnegative gradings on all effective motives; positivity of Hodge gradings on effective motives (h^{p,q} ≠ 0 only for p, q ≥ 0).
ideas.modern_name: Hodge cocharacter / Mumford–Tate cocharacter positivity; effective Hodge structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971; Shimura varieties, 1979); Serre's motivic Galois group conjectures (1994)

ideas.what: Attempt at a finiteness axiom on effective motives of given weight, self-questioned with '(??)'.
ideas.modern_name: Finiteness of Hodge types of effective weight-i structures (trivial), or finiteness of motives (false)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly translates 'effective motives' into a cone K^+(G) in the representation ring of the motivic Galois group, together with a notion of 'effective' cocharacters. This is exactly the data that, in the theory of reductive monoids (Vinberg, Putcha, Renner), classifies normal monoid schemes with unit group G. The page therefore implicitly contains the idea of a 'motivic Galois monoid' whose representations are the effective motives. This viewpoint has not, to my knowledge, been systematically developed (unsure).
missed.quote: donc une telle donnée de structure peut être considérée comme équivalente à la donnée d'un cône K^+(G) ... stable par produit
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A monoid-theoretic (Vinberg-monoid) description of effective motives could make conjectures about effectivity (e.g. effectivity of Hodge-theoretically effective motives, generalized Hodge conjecture of Grothendieck type) into statements about cones and cocharacters of the motivic Galois group.

missed.claim: Grothendieck lists positivity of Hodge gradings and effective cocharacters as candidate axioms linking the effectivity structure to Hodge theory. The precise axiom (boxed, marked '??') is left open.
missed.quote: Un hom. G_ℂ —i→ G_ℂ effectif si pour tout E ∈ Ob M^+, la graduation correspondante de E_ℂ est à [degrés positifs]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The question of which group-theoretic positivity data characterize effective motives (relevant to the generalized Hodge conjecture, i.e. the coniveau/level question) remains open.

deep.surprise_reason: Effective motives and Tate twisting are standard. The explicit Tannakian reformulation as a positive cone in K(G) plus 'effective cocharacters' is a nice unpublished detail anticipating monoid-theoretic viewpoints. But it is sketchy, partly crossed out, and the key axiom is self-doubted.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'sous-catégorie strict. pleine de M (motifs effectifs)', with 'strict. pleine' inserted above.
The insertion over the third line reads 'ou Λ(-1) soit effectif et que pour tout E', i.e. the Lefschetz motive is required to be effective.
'G_ℂ' in the line 'Une telle structure sur ... G_ℂ' is likely correct (complexified motivic Galois group); the verb is probably 'on définit une ... sur G_ℂ, et vice-versa'.

The boxed text likely reads: 'Axiome: Pour tout i il n'y a qu'un [nombre fini?] de types de motifs effectifs de poids i ... (??) En particulier ... motifs effectifs ... tels que G^0 ...'. The circled '(??)' marks doubt.
'positif' is crossed out and replaced by 'effectif' in 'Un hom. G_{m,ℂ} → G_ℂ effectif'; the source is probably G_m, not G.
The last line probably ends 'est à degrés ≥ 0' / 'à gradations positives'.
